newsitem.title: UK: Kingfisher, Boots lifted by Wickes statement.
newsitem.headline: Kingfisher, Boots lifted by Wickes statement.

text.p: Shares in retailers Kingfisher Plc and Boots Co Plc rose on Thursday, as strong results from Wickes Plc sparked hopes for their DIY operations, dealers said.

Other retailers also attracted interest after underperforming the rest of the market for the past six months. "They have underperformed and one or two people have looked at the sector and decided it's too cheap," said one market-maker.
Kingfisher, owner of the B&Q chain, was up 16-1/2p at 684-1/2 by 1334 GMT while Boots, which owns Do-it-All, was up 8p at 700. J Sainsbury Plc, which runs the Homebase chain, was up 2-1/2p at 334.
Earlier Wickes said like-for-like sales were up 14 percent in the 17 weeks to April 26. Total sales at the company were up 20 percent.
Wickes shares, which returned from a lengthy suspension on January 10, were up 10p at 176.

Among other retail stocks, Great Universal Stores Plc were up 16-1/2p at 654-1/2, Marks & Spencer Plc was up 3p at 493, Dixons Group Plc was up 5-1/2p at 511-1/2, WH Smith Plc was up 8p at 466 and Next Plc was up 4-1/2p at 656.
Retail stocks have languished in recent months amid speculation that rises in interest rates and taxes after today's UK election will dampen consumer spending and bear down on profits in the sector.
